02 · ACUPOINTUX/UI · International Workshop · 1st Place

A calmer way to spend the wait.

AcuPoint is a mobile concept designed around the acupuncture appointment experience, offering patients simple educational content, appointment information, after-care guidance and an opportunity to reflect on their visit.

Format
2-day design workshop
Location
Shanghai, China
Collaboration
Shuguang Hospital
Result
1st Place

Workshop context

Two days.
One focused challenge.

AcuPoint was developed during the Sanda–SRH Student Design Workshop in Shanghai, in collaboration with Shuguang Hospital. With only two days to develop the concept, the focus was on identifying an opportunity within the patient experience and translating it into a clear mobile solution.

Making waiting time a little more useful.

The concept explores how the time around an acupuncture appointment could feel more informative and supportive. AcuPoint gives patients access to short learning content and relevant appointment information, while also extending the experience into after-care and feedback.

The app experience

Designed around the appointment.

The interface follows different moments around the visit — from preparing for an appointment, to learning while waiting, to after-care and reflection afterwards.

Before the visit

Starting with how you feel.

The experience begins with a simple check-in, allowing patients to indicate what brings them to their appointment.

While waiting

A little context while you wait.

The home experience keeps the upcoming appointment visible while offering short educational content that patients can explore during their wait.

After the appointment

Care that continues beyond the visit.

After the appointment, the experience shifts toward simple after-care guidance, helping patients keep track of the information associated with their visit.

Feedback

Closing the loop.

The final part of the experience gives patients a simple way to reflect on the visit and share feedback.

Workshop outcome

From concept to exhibition.

At the end of the workshop, the project was presented as part of the Sanda–SRH Student Design Workshop exhibition in Shanghai.

Result

1st Place

Sanda–SRH Student Design Workshop

Reflection

What I took from it.

Working within a two-day workshop pushed me to make decisions quickly and focus on the core idea rather than trying to solve everything at once. It was also an opportunity to design within a new context, collaborate across an international workshop setting, and turn an early concept into something that could be presented by the end of the experience.
